concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper-bound notation for growth rates of running time.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Formal sums of powers of an indeterminate with coefficients in a ring or field.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a, b and i squared equal to -1.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, where each step moves each head by at most one cell.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: Exact integer multiplication
concepts.gloss: Computing the exact binary representation of the product of two n-bit integers, with no rounding.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture
concepts.gloss: The conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of growth for multiplying n-bit integers on a multitape Turing machine.

evidence.quote: proposed n log n as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: A linear map that evaluates a sequence at powers of a root of unity, computing convolutions pointwise after transformation.

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Multiplication of two coefficient sequences as polynomials modulo x^S - 1, so that exponents wrap around modulo S.

evidence.quote: convolution modulo xS − 1 has no nonzero wraparound

concepts.name: Radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Reduction of integer multiplication to a convolution of coefficient lists obtained by splitting each input into radix digits and propagating carries.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: A relabelling of a cyclic convolution of length S as a multidimensional cyclic convolution over pairwise coprime lengths, via the Chinese remainder theorem.

evidence.quote: Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: The ring of polynomials in y with coefficients in C, reduced modulo y^r + 1 for a power of two r, in which y^r = -1.

evidence.quote: a polynomial modulo y r + 1, with r a power of two

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A transform over a polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1 whose roots of unity are powers of y, so that multiplying by a root is a signed cyclic shift of coefficients.

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: A multiplication of coefficients by powers of a root zeta = e^(pi i / r) that converts cyclic wraparound in the last coordinate into negacyclic wraparound modulo y^r + 1, and back.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial

concepts.name: Address-field interchange
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that swaps two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in O(V u^tau) time for a fixed tau < 1, with intermediate XOR combinations but an exact final permutation.

evidence.quote: interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in an array

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that applies the two-point map H0(u, v) = ((u + v)/2, (u − v)/2) to selected coordinate bits of all records at once, in O(V d^lambda') time.

concepts.name: Linear networks with frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network that exchanges banks of values with prescribed signs and restores auxiliary values, where each node carries an invertible frame operator so that intermediate frames cancel along a route.

evidence.quote: choose an invertible linear operator Dv on the space of arrays

concepts.name: Subset-intersection subspace construction
concepts.gloss: A construction that attaches nested subspaces of a fixed space to the gates of a linear network, using three-element subsets and intersection-size parity, so that the subspace dimensions drop along each edge.

evidence.quote: attaches subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional space to its

concepts.name: Recursive rank saving
concepts.gloss: The recursion in which a call at parameter m uses s smaller calls with s < W m, so the cost per unit of volume is multiplied by a factor below m at each level and gives a power saving.

evidence.quote: that the total number s of smaller calls satisfies s < W m

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier
concepts.gloss: The known deterministic O(n log n) multitape multiplication, used as an ordinary subroutine on short records.

evidence.quote: Calls to the established O(n log n) multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing
concepts.gloss: Encoding polynomial coefficients as signed integers at a fixed bit spacing so that one integer multiplication computes a polynomial product in the ring modulo y^r + 1.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: The bookkeeping showing that fixed-precision approximations of the transforms recover each integer coefficient exactly after rounding, so that carry propagation yields the exact product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below 1/2

concepts.name: Parameter choice
concepts.gloss: The fixed rational exponents and the sizes b, p, d, T and r chosen so that the cost terms all fit the target bound.

evidence.quote: Take the power of two T in [4n/b, 8n/b)

concepts.name: Multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: The six-step algorithm that forms three source transforms, multiplies them pointwise, scales and rounds the result, and propagates carries to output the exact 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote: The source-transform procedures now supply the three transforms needed for the radix-digit convolution.

concepts.name: Cost accounting
concepts.gloss: The normalized cost table showing each operation costs O(T p) times a power of p, and that every exponent falls below one by a margin of at least 2^(-181) = 2 kappa.

concepts.name: Deterministic O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)) multiplication
concepts.gloss: There is one deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine computing the exact product of n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)) worst-case time, with kappa = 2^(-182), which refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: There is one deterministic Turing machine A, with a fixed finite alphabet

concepts.name: Bit complexity
concepts.gloss: The running time of an algorithm measured as the number of elementary bit-level steps on a fixed machine model, as opposed to arithmetic operations on words.

evidence.quote: the algorithm is intended to establish a bit-complexity bound

concepts.name: Centred extraction
concepts.gloss: Recovering each packed coefficient as the representative in a window centred at zero, so that a signed coefficient is not confused with a large positive one.

evidence.quote: Signed packing, centered extraction, negacyclic wrapping, and copying are linear stream passes

concepts.name: Array with a complete Cartesian address set
concepts.gloss: An array whose addresses are all tuples in a product of ranges, stored in lexicographic order with the first coordinate most significant.

evidence.quote: is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant

concepts.name: Linear convolution
aliases: ordinary polynomial product of coefficient lists
concepts.gloss: The coefficient list of the ordinary product of two polynomials, with no reduction modulo any polynomial, so its length is the sum of the input lengths minus one.

concepts.name: Fixed tracks
concepts.gloss: Additional fixed rows of a tape that store extra data in parallel with the main data, so that a fixed number of tracks changes the running time only by a constant factor.

evidence.quote: Fixed tracks and finitely many work tapes change time by a fixed factor

concepts.name: Frankl–Wilson construction
aliases: Alon's presentation of the Frankl–Wilson construction
concepts.gloss: A construction of set systems with restricted intersection sizes, which gives low-degree polynomial representations of intersection graphs over fields.

evidence.quote: presentation of the Frankl–Wilson construction [9] gives low-degree representations of complementary intersection graphs over different fields

concepts.name: Gather and scatter operations
concepts.gloss: Operations that collect the entries of a network's wires over a three-element subset and redistribute them, producing coefficients that depend only on the size of the intersection of two subsets.

evidence.quote: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadic numbers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are dyadic rationals, that is, have denominators that are powers of two.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

concepts.name: Disk-grid values
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers stored exactly with p fractional bits in each real and imaginary part, with norm bounded by a fixed constant.

evidence.quote: Their coefficients are exact p-bit grid values of norm less than 1/4

concepts.name: Indicator vector
concepts.gloss: A vector indexed by a ground set whose entry is 1 at the elements of a given subset and 0 elsewhere.

concepts.name: Linear contraction
concepts.gloss: A linear map that does not increase the size of its inputs, so that its output has norm at most that of the input.

evidence.quote: The ordered Gaussian resampling maps are contractions

concepts.name: Normalized cost
concepts.gloss: The running time of an operation divided by the stored volume V, so that costs of different operations on arrays of different sizes can be compared as powers of p.

evidence.quote: Table 1 lists costs after division by V

concepts.name: Record
concepts.gloss: A fixed-width block of stored data, such as one polynomial with complex coefficients, that is handled as a single unit by the procedures.

evidence.quote: Each record is a polynomial with complex fixed-point coefficients

concepts.name: Row of an array
concepts.gloss: The block of consecutive entries that share a fixed prefix and row index, containing all address fields after the row field.

evidence.quote: regard a row as the complete ordered suffix, including all active address fields, at a fixed prefix and row index

concepts.name: Sup norm
concepts.gloss: The maximum absolute value of the coefficients of a polynomial or array.

evidence.quote: Both exact maps preserve the coefficient sup norm

concepts.name: Linear index-code decoding
concepts.gloss: Recovering a wanted coordinate from a low-rank linear summary of several coordinates by subtracting the contributions of neighbouring coordinates that are already known.

evidence.quote: a low-rank linear summary gives the wanted coordinate plus contributions from known neighboring coordinates

concepts.name: Middle transform
concepts.gloss: The central factor in the splitting of a source Fourier transform into Gaussian resampling, a chirp, and this middle transform, which the chirp identity then converts into a convolution.

evidence.quote: We next use the complex convolution to evaluate the middle factor QFt in (35)

concepts.name: Complex modulus (norm of a coefficient)
concepts.gloss: For a complex number x + iy, its modulus sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the length of the number viewed as a vector in the plane, which is the norm used to bound each coefficient.

evidence.quote: Their coefficients are exact p-bit grid values of norm less than 1/4.

concepts.name: Rational bilinear form
concepts.gloss: A function of two vectors that is linear in each argument separately and whose coefficients are rational numbers.

evidence.quote: We change the ground-set size and express the second pairing through a rational bilinear form.

concepts.name: Source and target permutations
concepts.gloss: The reorderings of the coordinates of a transform's input and output that the transform identity keeps symbolically instead of executing as separate sorts.

evidence.quote: Section 8 retains the source and target coordinate permutations in the transform identity

concepts.name: Transform identity
concepts.gloss: The identity that expresses each source Fourier transform, after Gaussian resampling, through a power-of-two tensor transform together with source and target coordinate permutations.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform

concepts.name: Complementary intersection graphs
concepts.gloss: A pair of graphs on the same family of sets, one joining two sets when their intersection size lies in a prescribed set of values and the other joining the remaining pairs, so that each is the complement of the other.

evidence.quote: gives low-degree representations of complementary intersection graphs over different fields

concepts.name: Side wire
concepts.gloss: A wire of a linear network that joins two neighbouring triples of the construction, carrying values between them in addition to the central wires and the data wires.

evidence.quote: On a side wire joining neighboring physical triples
